title: Fairness of Explanations in Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Unifying Framework, Axioms, and Future Direction toward Responsible AI
abstract: arXiv:2605.09852v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Machine learning algorithms are being used in high-stakes decisions, including those in criminal justice, healthcare, credit, and employment. The research community has responded with two largely independent research fields: \emph{algorithmic fairness}, which targets equitable outcomes, and \emph{explainable AI} (XAI), which targets interpretable reasoning. This survey identifies and maps a novel blind spot at their intersection, which is a model that can satisfy every standard fairness criterion in its outputs while being profoundly unfair in its \emph{reasoning process}. We refer to this as the procedural bias, and mitigating it requires treating the fairness of explanations as a distinct object of scientific study.   To our knowledge, we provide the first unified theoretical and literature review of this emerging field and elucidate the drawbacks of post-hoc explainers in certifying explanation fairness. translated_title: 人工智能（AI）解释的公平性：统一框架、公理与迈向负责任人工智能的未来方向
translated_abstract: 机器学习算法正被应用于高风险决策领域，包括刑事司法、医疗保健、信贷和就业等。研究界为此发展出了两个彼此较为独立的研究领域：算法公平性，旨在实现公平的结果；以及可解释人工智能（XAI），旨在实现可解释的推理。本综述识别并描绘了这两个领域交叉处的一个新颖盲点：即一个模型可能在输出上满足所有标准公平性准则，但其推理过程却存在深刻的不公平性。我们将此现象称为程序性偏见，要缓解这一问题，就需要将解释的公平性作为一个独立的科学研究对象。据我们所知，我们提供了对这一新兴领域的首个统一的理论与文献综述，并阐明了事后解释器在认证解释公平性方面的缺陷。我们的核心贡献...
tldr: 本文首次提出了研究AI解释公平性的统一理论框架与公理体系，揭示了模型即使输出满足公平性标准，其推理过程仍可能存在“程序性偏见”，并为迈向负责任的人工智能指明了未来方向。
en_tdlr: This paper provides the first unified theoretical framework and literature review for the fairness of AI explanations, identifying "procedural bias" where models can satisfy fairness criteria in outputs while being profoundly unfair in their reasoning processes, and outlines future directions toward responsible AI.
